dedupe_keys.name: solar storms and submarine internet cables line voltage monitoring of four transoceanic systems castellanos et al 2022

description: This preprint measures voltage changes in the power supply of four different transoceanic submarine cables during periods of high solar activity to gauge how coronal mass ejections and geomagnetic storms threaten internet cables. It finds a strong correlation between the strength of the high-frequency geomagnetic field at the landing sites and the line voltage change, and a near-linear power-law scaling that allows estimating effects of once-in-a-century events. It concludes that long-haul submarine cables, regardless of length and orientation, will not be damaged during a solar superstorm, even one as large as the 1859 Carrington event. Producer: Jorge Castellanos, Jo Conroy, Valey Kamalov, Mattia Cantono and Urs Hölzle, posted 15 November 2022 (19 pages, 5 figures). Coverage: four transoceanic cable systems. Access: paper on arXiv; no data files were read on the abstract page. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC0-1.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: results cover four systems and only the abstract page was read, so statistics and data were not checked. Simulation uses: the scaling law supports hazard and resilience models of cable-powered networks under space weather. Related records: none linked.
